model_meta.description: Concept-level model of the claimed differential gear, its helical torque path, thrust-bearing arrangements, and direction-dependent differential-limiting behavior.

subsystems.description: Receives driving force at the assembly boundary, holds pinion gearing, and axially supports output gears through inward support faces opposing outward annular counter faces across the first gap; inward counter faces oppose one another across the second gap.

One or more helical pinion gears are arranged on an axis parallel to the differential case rotation axis and rotatably held in a hole formed inside the case. They mesh with the helical output gears; the disclosed paired arrangement also has the pinions mesh with each other.
functional_basis: create axial thrust through helix geometry

subsystems.description: Mesh with pinion gearing and output driving forces. Helix geometry produces direction-dependent axial thrust on the gears, which is reacted through the supported counter-face and thrust-bearing arrangement.

Radially arranged rollers between annular plates. Interposed in at least one alternative gap: first-gap plates contact case support and output outward counter faces; second-gap plates contact inward counter faces. First-direction loading causes specified sliding to produce differential-limiting force; second-direction loading through the bearing reduces sliding resistance.

parts.description: Plurality of rollers arranged radially with respect to the inward and outward counter faces.
Pair of annular plates contacting opposing faces at the selected gap; the radial inner end of one plate is radially and directly supported by one helical output gear.

item_flows.name: Input driving force/rotation
item_flows.notes: Driving force reaches the differential case through an upstream propeller shaft, meshing ring gear, and drive pinion gear; these upstream elements are external context, not a direct shaft-to-case interface.

item_flows.name: Gear-transmitted driving force
item_flows.notes: Transferred from case through pinions to the paired output gears.

item_flows.name: Differential output driving forces
item_flows.notes: Driving forces output by the paired helical output gears; no downstream shaft connection is asserted.

item_flows.name: Direction-dependent axial thrust
item_flows.notes: Internal mechanical axial effect generated by helical gear meshing: output gears are urged apart or toward one another depending on case-turn direction, and thrust is reacted at the case support/counter faces and, where interposed, the thrust-bearing plates and rollers; distinct from rotary gear-transfer connections.

actions.name: Transmit torque and generate direction-dependent limiting behavior

steps.description: The differential case receives driving force and rotates the pinion gear set.
The helical pinion gears mesh with the paired helical output gears and transmit driving forces to them.
Helix geometry produces axial thrust on the output gears; the direction of case rotation determines whether the gears are urged apart or together.

In the first direction gears move toward the first gap and either outward counter faces slide on case support faces or inward counter faces slide on each other, producing differential-limiting force. In the second direction gears move toward the second gap and faces are loaded through the thrust bearing, reducing sliding resistance.
